carla: Quick heads-up — I have a reproducible case where KV pages fragment and memory keeps growing with INT8 enabled on long contexts (>=32k). Repro uses llama-13b-fp16->int8 conversion + our paging layer. :eyes:
ben: Can you share the top-line numbers? How bad is the growth?
carla: Baseline (bf16 kernel): ~0.9GB/session after 32k tokens. With our INT8 path: steady growth to ~2.3GB/session over same run. Eviction happens but free list never reuses a lot of those slots — lots of small holes.
alice: Interesting. Any accuracy delta with INT8 on that longctx workload?
carla: Yes — eval on our chat prompts: INT8 quant gives ~2.9% token-level next-token loss regress vs BF16 on the longer prefix set. Short contexts (<2k) look fine.
dan: Do we know if it's the quantized KV layout (packed vs padded) or the runtime copy path?
carla: I instrumented allocation shapes: most holes are from pages freed mid-sequence when we evict older kv segments. Packed INT8 slices end up with varying sizes per layer due to per-head quant block rounding; our buddy allocator doesn't coalesce across size classes.
ben: Got it. So fragmentation + heterogenous small allocations. Any correlation with kernel change we rolled last week?
carla: Yes — the new attention kernel switched to a temp-copy that shaves compute but adds an extra allocation per forward when reading paged KV. On BF16 that overhead is amortized; on INT8 the bitpacked loads + temp buffer cause slightly different free patterns and increase churn.

infra-bot: deploy-breakdown: runtime/attention-kernel v3.4.1 deployed 2025-07-30 03:22 UTC to canary (50%)

alice: So two axes: (A) allocator/coalescing, (B) kernel copy path producing different free ordering. Priorities?
carla: My vote: quick mitigation -> periodic compaction pass to merge free holes, TTL on old prefix caches, and revert the temp-copy in the attention kernel on canary while we investigate.
ben: Can you sketch the compaction idea? Cheap and safe?
carla: Yeah. Prototype script: kv_compactor.py runs in-process during low load window and does: scan free lists -> build bucketed move list -> allocate contiguous pages -> remap layer pointers -> atomic swap. It's intrusive but we can do it as an opt-in background task. Snippet:
```
# pseudo
for layer in model.layers:
    free_chunks = allocator.list_free(layer)
    if fragmentation_score(free_chunks) > 0.25:
        target = allocator.alloc_contiguous(sum(sizes))
        copy_chunks(free_chunks, target)
        update_kv_ptrs(layer, mapping)
```
This reduces fragmentation in my local run from ~45% to <8%.

alice: Nice. Risks: pointer swaps must be atomic wrt inference threads. We'll need a short stall or a freelist swap handshake.
dan: Alternatively, change allocator to use size-class defrag (periodic slab compaction) — longer project but safer for hot paths.
carla: Agreed. For short-term I propose: 1) revert canary kernel change, 2) enable background compactor opt-in for a limited tenant, 3) add telemetry for per-layer fragmentation + allocation histograms.
ben: Also add an INT8-specific allocator path that uses fixed-size pages per layer (avoid small variable slices). That might cost a bit more memory but reduces fragmentation a ton.

carla: On accuracy tradeoffs: we saw ~3% loss on longprefix. Hypothesis: INT8 KV quant noise compounds over long recency windows — caching/reuse amplifies it. We should run ablations: INT8 weights + BF16 kv, BF16 weights + INT8 kv, and mixed precision (KV in BF16 but activations int8).
alice: Good call. Can you queue those three experiments and paste results here? Put them under the longctx eval harness.
carla: Will do. Early quick numbers: BF16-kv + INT8-weights reduces loss delta to ~1.1%. Mixed (BF16 kv, INT8 activations) is ~0.9% but memory savings are only ~30% vs 55% for full INT8.

dan: That's actionable — for regulated tenants we can offer a mixed profile: keep KV at bf16, quant weights/activations to int8 to save compute but avoid kv noise.
ben: Ops items: (a) add fragmentation histos + per-layer allocations to console, (b) gate kernel change until we have atomic pointer swap, (c) test compactor on staging and 1 tenant.
carla: I'll open a PR with the compactor and the telemetry dashboard patch. Also adding a short benchmark script: run longctx-loop + smoke eval to capture loss drift over time.
alice: Thanks. @ben @dan please ack if you can do the kernel revert + console metrics this sprint.
ben: Ack — I'll do kernel revert and canary rollback today.
dan: Ack — will add allocation histograms to tracing next 48h.
carla: Filing follow-ups: GH#5124 compactor prototype, GH#5125 int8-ablation harness, TASK-984 kernel revert. I'll link results here once experiments finish. :thumbsup:
